new.n: Hunch: Koster's farm? Unnamed 80 acres, south-central sec. 21, Sac Bay (Garden peninsula)
new.y: 1909 (house burned); tract blank on the 1913 atlas
new.pl: Unnamed 80 in the south-central part of sec. 21 T38N R19W (Fairbanks Twp), read as SE1/4 SW1/4 + SW1/4 SE1/4 (BLM PLSS)

why: 3 Feb 1909: the aged recluse who lived alone at 'Garden' died when his house burned; his fortune was said to be hidden in the house, and no find was ever reported.
The 1900 census (Sack Bay Twp) lists him between the McGregor and Thomson households (sec. 19 T38N R19W in the 1913 Delta atlas patrons list) and the Watchorn and Ronkey households (sec. 21).

The 1913 Standard Atlas of Delta County (p. 52) has no Koster tract, but he had died in 1909. In that cluster only two private-looking tracts carry no name: an 80 in south-central sec. 21 (this pin) and a 160 in the SW quarter of sec. 22.
A blank tract four years after a lone man's death fits an unsettled estate. That makes this 80 one of two candidates for his home farm.
inf.yes: A Delta County deed, tax roll or probate naming Koster or his estate on this 80; a 1909 item naming the section; a cellar hole inside the 80 on LiDAR or the 1938-40 air photos.
inf.no: The deed or tax record shows another owner on this 80 in 1900-1913, or a record puts his house in another section.

new.st: Inferred hunch, not a record: A blank tract four years after a lone man's death fits an unsettled estate. That makes this 80 one of two candidates for his home farm.
new.t: check the record first (see Would confirm it) before any trip. Private land: ask the owner. The hunch ring is about 450 m.

new.n: Hunch: 'above the point' = Ketchum's Point, foot of old Mac Street, Portage
new.pl: Wisconsin River bank at Portage from the foot of Cass St to the foot of the old Mac St (Mac St lay one block E of Dunn St; foot about 43.5378,-89.4651)

why: 9 Apr 1887 (Portage paper, 16 Apr): old half-dollars, one dated 1828, washed out of the left bank of the Wisconsin 'above the point' at Portage; over $100 was dug before the river rose.

Turner, The Family Tree of Columbia County (1904): before about 1850 one branch of the portage trail climbed 'the high land at Ketchum's Point' and reached the Wisconsin 'near the foot of Mac street'. It is the only named point on the Wisconsin side at Portage found so far.

The 1878 Snyder, Van Vechten plate of Portage shows Mac Street running down to the river one block east of Dunn Street. Mac St is gone today, so its foot is set from the Dunn and Cass street ends (OpenStreetMap) by the block spacing.
A traveller's purse buried where the old trail met the river fits the 1887 guess that 'some early traveller' hid it. The ring covers the town bank from Cass to Mac.
inf.yes: A map or history that labels Ketchum's Point; a follow-up 1887 item naming the street, the property or the finder.
inf.no: 'The point' proves to be the canal mouth or another bend; or 'left bank' meant the south (4th ward) bank, which is the left bank going downstream.

new.st: Inferred hunch, not a record: A traveller's purse buried where the old trail met the river fits the 1887 guess that 'some early traveller' hid it. The ring covers the town bank from Cass to Mac.

new.n: Hunch: D. K. Smalling's farm lay in Mount Vernon Township (Black Hawk Co.)
new.pl: Mount Vernon civil township, Black Hawk Co., NE of Cedar Falls (township centre; ring covers the township)

why: Aug 1904: nearly $300 in coin came up at the old granary site on the D. K. Smalling farm 'near Cedar Falls'; it was believed buried by a Civil War soldier who never came back for it.
The 1900 census has D. K. Smalling in Mount Vernon Twp, Black Hawk Co. (ED 16, sheet 8, dwelling 150), four years before the find.
So the farm was most likely in Mount Vernon Twp, about 10 km NE of Cedar Falls, not at the town itself. (An Ira Smalling in sec. 6 near Janesville in 1878 is a different man.)
inf.yes: The Mount Vernon Twp plate of the 1896 or 1910 Black Hawk atlas: the tract among his 1900 census neighbours (Repp, Bowen, G. W. Phelps, N. Fitkin, J. Hartman, F. Webster, R. Schmidt, Z. T. Aikey). He may have rented, so look for the owner's land.
inf.no: He moved between 1900 and 1904 (the 1905 Iowa census or a directory puts him elsewhere).

new.n: Hunch: 'the old Patrick Callahan farm' lay in Lafayette Township (Allamakee Co.)
new.pl: Lafayette civil township, Allamakee Co., about 8 km SE of Lansing (township centre; ring covers the township)

why: May 1921: a farm hand plowed up a glass fruit jar of gold coins (about $1,300) in a field on 'the old Patrick Callahan farm near Lansing'.
The 1900 census has Patrick Callahan, farmer, owning his farm free of mortgage, in Lafayette Twp, Allamakee Co. (ED 7, sheet 1, dwelling 6). A second man, Patrick H. Callahan, is in Iowa Twp.
A farm owner 21 years earlier is the best fit for 'the old Patrick Callahan farm', so the field is most likely in Lafayette Twp.
inf.yes: The Lafayette Twp plate of the 1886 or 1917 Allamakee atlas: Callahan next to his 1900 neighbours Tisdale, Kean, Steiber and Goebble.
inf.no: No Callahan on the Lafayette plate, or the 1921 papers name the Iowa Twp man.

new.n: Hunch: Herman Ludtke's hidden money, Palermo Township (Grundy Co.)
new.pl: Palermo civil township, Grundy Co., beside Grundy Center (township centre; ring covers the township)

why: Aug 1907: Herman Ludtke, a musician and Grundy Center 'man of mystery', died at the county poor farm; he was thought to have hidden money.
The 1900 census has 'Herman Ludke' renting in Palermo Twp, Grundy Co. (ED 45, sheet 2, dwelling 38); there is no other Ludtke or Ludke in the county.
If he hid money, the likeliest place is where he lived before the poor farm, which points to Palermo Twp. As a renter he will not be on a plat.
inf.yes: A 1900-07 Grundy Center paper naming where he lived, or a later find.
inf.no: He lived in town after 1900, or the money was found when he died.

new.n: Hunch: Hein's logging camp (Bish photos c.1895-1904) was near Tony
new.pl: Tony, Rusk Co. (Chippewa Co. until 1901); the 1901-05 plat shows a saw mill in sec. 33 T35N R5W

why: The Wisconsin Historical Society holds A. A. Bish photos of 'Hein's logging camp' (c.1895, 'largest load ever hauled by four horses', and 1904 views with a railroad log crane), tagged only 'Chippewa County'.
Tony lay in Chippewa County until Gates (now Rusk) County was split off in 1901, so a c.1895 photo of a Tony camp would be filed under Chippewa County.
The only Hein logging firm in our sources is the John Hein Co. at Tony (Chronicling America, 1916). The Clark Co. 'Hein' mill (1893 plat, sec. 5 T25N R1W) is a name match in the wrong county.
inf.yes: A Chippewa Herald or Ladysmith paper item naming Hein's camp with a creek or section; a Chippewa County Historical Society caption; a Hein Co. start at Tony before 1901.
inf.no: The Hein company came to Tony after 1904, or a caption places the camp elsewhere in today's Chippewa County.

new.n: Hunch: Eau Claire Lumber Co. North Fork camps, around its sec. 23 dam
new.pl: Around the Eau Claire Lumber Co. dam, sec. 23 T29N R5W (1888 Chippewa plat), North Fork of the Eau Claire River

why: The Eau Claire Lumber Co. drove logs down the North Fork of the Eau Claire River; the Daily Free Press (15 Apr 1878) reports 'the Company's flooding dam on the North Fork' damaged.
The 1888 Chippewa County plat shows an Eau Claire Lumber Co. dam in sec. 23 T29N R5W.
Winter camps sat near the drive streams and landings they served, and a dam needed a tender, so the dam is the best anchor for the company's camps. No named camp has been found yet.
inf.yes: A named camp in the Eau Claire or Chippewa papers or the company papers (UWEC Special Collections); a camp clearing, root cellar or dump on the 1938 air photos or LiDAR near the dam.
inf.no: Company papers that put its North Fork camps on another stretch.

new.n: Hunch: Sterling and Leonard logging camp (1884), North Fork near Thorp
new.pl: North Fork of the Eau Claire River in the town of Thorp, around the Mississippi River Logging Co. dam, sec. 27 T29N R4W (1893 Clark plat)

why: Eau Claire Leader, 6 Dec 1884: 'Jos. Sterling, of Thorp, has organized a logging camp on the North Fork of the Eau Claire with Dave Leonard', to put in four million feet.
The nearest mapped North Fork works to Thorp village are the Mississippi River Logging Co. dam in sec. 27 T29N R4W, town of Thorp (1893 plat), about 5 km west of the village.
A Thorp man's camp on the North Fork most likely sat in the town of Thorp, so the ring is centred on that dam.
inf.yes: A Clark County Republican or Thorp Courier item placing the camp (WHS microfilm), or a camp clearing on the 1938 air photos or LiDAR.
inf.no: A source placing the camp on the North Fork upstream in Taylor County or downstream in Chippewa County.
